title: Video basics: frames, fps and temporal latents

questions.q: Five seconds at 24 fps is 120 frames. By the lab's formulas, how many frames come back after encoding and decoding with a temporal factor of 4?
options: 120, nothing is lost
117, from 30 latent frames
121, the length is rounded up
30, one frame per latent frame
questions.why: Latent frames = (120 − 1) // 4 + 1 = 30, and decoding gives 4 · 30 − 3 = 117. Only lengths of the form 1 + 4m come back unchanged.

questions.q: Why is a length of 121 frames valid for temporal factors 4, 6 and 8 at the same time?
options: Because 121 is a prime number
Because 121 = 1 + 120, and 120 is a multiple of 4, 6 and 8
Because every model uses 121 frames
Because 121 is the square of 11, so it divides evenly
questions.answer: Because 121 = 1 + 120, and 120 is a multiple of 4, 6 and 8
questions.why: A length survives the round trip when it is 1 + k · m. The lab shows 121 coming back as 121 for k = 4, 6 and 8, while 120 comes back as 117, 115 and 113.

questions.q: What is the latent shape that WanImageToVideo creates at its defaults of 832 × 480 and 81 frames?
questions.why: 16 channels, (81 − 1) // 4 + 1 = 21 latent frames, and 480 / 8 = 60 by 832 / 8 = 104 in space.

questions.q: Why is the Wan 2.1 default clip compressed by 46.29 and not by the long-clip limit of 48?
options: The VAE loses 4% of the frames
The first frame has a latent frame to itself, so 21 latent frames stand for 81 frames and not 84
The width is not a multiple of 16
Because 48 only applies to fp8 models
questions.answer: The first frame has a latent frame to itself, so 21 latent frames stand for 81 frames and not 84
questions.why: The limit 3 · 4 · 8 · 8 / 16 = 48 assumes every latent frame covers 4 frames. 48 · 81 / 84 = 46.29, the lab's figure. The Wan paper says the first frame is only spatially compressed.

questions.q: Doubling Wan's clip from 81 to 161 frames multiplied the tokens by 1.95 and the attention pairs by 3.81 in the lab. Why not 2 and 4?
options: Attention is cheaper than quadratic
161 frames is 41 latent frames, and 41 / 21 = 1.95. Squaring that gives 3.81
The lab rounds all numbers down
Tokens are only counted for the first half of the clip
questions.answer: 161 frames is 41 latent frames, and 41 / 21 = 1.95. Squaring that gives 3.81
questions.why: Latent frames are (n − 1) // 4 + 1, so the lone first frame makes 81 → 21 and 161 → 41. Tokens scale with latent frames and attention pairs with their square.

questions.q: What does the fps value of CreateVideo do?
options: It changes how many frames the model generates
It sets the playback rate of the frames you give it, so the duration is frames divided by fps
It sets the temporal factor of the VAE
It is the model's temporal conditioning for every video family
questions.answer: It sets the playback rate of the frames you give it, so the duration is frames divided by fps
questions.why: CreateVideo takes images and an fps. The latent shape does not depend on it. Some models, such as LTXV through LTXVConditioning, are also given a separate frame_rate in the conditioning.
